analysis.investment_thesis: Aegis Vopak is a quality LPG/chemical terminalling infrastructure business with excellent margins, but at INR 22,244 Cr market cap and 109x P/E, it is structurally incompatible with the SMILE framework — the price has already discounted decades of growth. Finance costs of INR 193 Cr nearly 1.5x the INR 127 Cr net profit signal capital allocation inefficiency despite operating strength.
key_strengths: Exceptional operating margins (48.5%) and gross margins (99.3%) — classic toll-road/infrastructure economics with recurring offtake revenue
Promoter holding at 86.94% — extraordinary skin in the game, strong alignment
FCF finally turned positive in FY25 (INR 350 Cr) after heavy capex phase, and OCF growing 353→621 Cr revenue trajectory
key_risks: Valuation is punishing: P/E 109x, EV/EBITDA 55.84x, P/S 31.39x — zero margin of safety even in a bull case
Finance costs (INR 193 Cr) exceed net profit (INR 127 Cr), meaning debt is consuming nearly all operating gains
ROE only 8.73% and ROCE 7.01% — poor capital efficiency for an asset-heavy business at this premium valuation
red_flags: Market cap INR 22,244 Cr — 20x outside Kedia SMILE sweet spot of 100-1000 Cr; no information asymmetry edge here
P/E of 109x violates every value principle — forward P/E 42x still 3x too expensive for small-cap entry discipline
Interest burden nearly outweighs net profit — financial leverage risk in a rate-sensitive infrastructure business
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aegis Vopak is structurally a fine business — a terminalling and storage duopoly asset backed by Vopak's global expertise, with near-100% gross margins and growing OCF (INR 478 Cr in FY25). The revenue ramp from zero in FY22 to INR 621 Cr in FY25 reflects rapid asset commissioning, and the positive FCF of INR 350 Cr in FY25 marks the first real fruits of the capex cycle. The promoter holding of 86.94% is one of the best in the market. But this is where my enthusiasm ends.

The SMILE framework demands small size with large aspiration — Aegis Vopak already IS large, at INR 22,244 Cr. The market has already priced in the entire 10-year transformation. With P/E of 109x and ROCE of just 7%, you are paying world-class multiples for sub-par capital returns. The INR 193 Cr annual finance cost dwarfing INR 127 Cr net profit tells me that equity holders are, in effect, working for the lenders. For the SMILE investor, this is a company to admire from a distance — it may have been a multibagger entry point when it was a 200-500 Cr market cap story in 2021-22. Today, the margin of safety is absent and the size disqualifies it entirely from my framework.
